learningObjective: Explain the design and cost of a CPU fallback path when the compiler encounters an op with no GPU implementation.

canonicalClaims.claim: CPU fallback executes an unsupported op on the host by copying inputs D2H, running the CPU kernel, then copying outputs H2D before the next GPU op resumes; the PCIe round-trip can dominate the op's own cost for fine-grained ops.
conditions: The op has no GPU implementation.
nonImplications: Does not imply CPU fallback is always the wrong choice; some ops are inherently CPU-appropriate.
Does not imply that PCIe cost dominates for large ops.

misconceptions.claim: GPUs can emulate CPU code natively via compatibility SMs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No such hardware feature exists; GPUs execute only kernels compiled for them.

misconceptions.claim: Missing ops are silently dropped by the runtime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Runtimes fail loudly or fall back; they do not silently omit computation.

misconceptions.claim: Dual CPU+GPU execution is the standard fallback pattern.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only one implementation is executed for correctness; dual execution would double cost with no benefit.

misconceptions.claim: CPU fallback has constant overhead independent of tensor size.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PCIe copy cost scales with bytes transferred; larger tensors imply larger fallback cost.
